snapshot: Watchlist CivicState: code exists, but business status waits on paid beta proof.
briefThesis: CivicState is code-real but not investible until conversion, coverage, and delivery are proven.

authority.note: POM soul-review + wrk.dog merge constitute adoption - operator ruling 2026-06-12; see the PR's POM record

adoption.note: POM soul-review + wrk.dog merge constitute adoption - operator ruling 2026-06-12; see the PR's POM record

methods: Read existing planning and master-plan files.
Inspected representative web, API, worker, Prisma, payment, officials, delivery, and test files.
Cited repo and registry files as evidence.
Tagged external market claims and future outcomes as assumptions because network research was unavailable.

thesisCurrent.label: watchlist personal/research asset
thesisCurrent.summary: CivicState has a code-real civic-letter workflow, but no validated paid demand, coverage, or deliverability proof.
thesisCurrent.operatorConstraint: Registry says personal/research asset and asks operator to confirm whether it should pitch as a business [evidence: registry dispatch].

customerDefinition.primary: Individual U.S. resident with a specific civic concern, desired outcome, and ZIP code [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md; apps/api/src/routes/submissions.ts].
customerDefinition.excluded: Legal advice, claim filing, business advocacy, lobbying-firm work, harassment, threats, and automated follow-up campaigns [evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md; .planning/PROJECT.md].

marketSizing.approach: Bottom-up validation model; no top-down TAM claimed [assumption: workspace-only mode prevents current external market research].
marketSizing.betaProof: $1,500 from 100 paid submissions at $15 AOV [assumption: beta sample and tier mix; evidence: apps/api/src/routes/payments.ts].
marketSizing.narrowConsumerCase: $450,000 annual revenue from 25 metros x 1,000 paid submissions x $18 AOV [assumption: metro playbook; evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md for $18 month-12 ARPP].
marketSizing.largerOption: $4,000,000 annual revenue from 100 metros x 2,000 paid submissions x $20 AOV [assumption: national metro expansion; evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md for $20 month-24 ARPP].

revenueModel.codeGap: Checkout route uses fixed tiers and does not calculate live fee-inclusive margin [evidence: apps/api/src/routes/payments.ts].

competition: Manual official email/contact forms [assumption: common free substitute]

goToMarket.initialMotion: One-metro operator-recruited beta before SEO [assumption: sequencing derived from BUSINESS.md].
channels: Operator network and local civic communities [assumption: beta acquisition path]
Issue-specific local pages after paid delivery proof [evidence: .planning/GENESIS.md]
No paid acquisition before conversion and deliverability are measured [evidence: .planning/GENESIS.md]

risksAntiPlan: Users may not pay because manual official email is free [assumption: free substitute].
Local official lookup is a stub that returns an empty array [evidence: apps/api/src/lib/officials/cicero.ts].
Congress.gov path sets official email to empty, weakening the delivery promise [evidence: apps/api/src/lib/officials/congress.ts].
Government deliverability may fail despite Postmark and DNS controls [assumption: external inbox risk; evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md].
AI citation errors or weak source coverage can undermine the core trust claim [assumption: AI risk; evidence: apps/worker/src/agents/researcher.ts].
Registry identity mismatch can make external pitch confusing [evidence: registry dispatch; package.json].

assumptionLedger.assumption: Users will pay $5 to $25 for civic-letter delivery [assumption: unvalidated demand].
assumptionLedger.basis: Implemented tiers and project thesis [evidence: apps/api/src/routes/payments.ts; .planning/PROJECT.md].

assumptionLedger.assumption: Fixed pricing preserves margins [assumption: actual COGS not measured].
Official coverage can meet 95% federal/state and 60% local targets [assumption: API coverage unproven].
One operator can clear exceptions within 24 hours [assumption: workload unproven].

holes: No legal/compliance counsel memo found [assumption: workspace audit].
Official data coverage is incomplete [evidence: apps/api/src/lib/officials/cicero.ts; apps/api/src/lib/officials/congress.ts].
mitigations: Closed beta with conversion and delivery gates.
Human review of flagged and all-citation-failed submissions.
residualRisks: Officials may opt out or treat AI-aided letters as spam.
Compliance costs may exceed the thin consumer price point.
Market may be too small without organization/API wedge.

staleSignals: .planning/existing-state.md says zero app code exists, but apps and packages now contain implementation [evidence: .planning/existing-state.md; package.json].
.planning/ROADMAP.md marks all phases complete while .planning/STATE.md says Phase 1 is current [evidence: .planning/ROADMAP.md; .planning/STATE.md].
MASTER_PLAN.md discusses dynamic pricing while implemented payments use fixed tiers [evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md; apps/api/src/routes/payments.ts].

docDates.masterPlan: 2026-03-01 [assumption: MASTER_PLAN.md month-level date normalized to first day of month]

operatorQuestions: Should the registry present this as CivicState, brooks-history, or another name?
Should this remain a personal/research asset or be pitched as a business?
Who signs off on legal/compliance posture before public launch?
